content: The Tao Brush is a specialized medical instrument designed for an alternative method of performing endometrial biopsies. Unlike the traditional approach, which utilizes a catheter (commonly the Pipelle) to suction a portion of the uterine lining, the Tao Brush employs a small, flexible brush to gently sweep the entire inner surface of the uterus. This method allows for a more comprehensive sampling of the uterine lining, removes less tissue, and is associated with reduced pain compared to the conventional technique. Endometrial cancer is the most prevalent malignancy affecting the female reproductive system, according to the American Cancer Society. In 2007, approximately 39,080 new cases were expected, with around 7,400 women in the United States projected to die from uterine cancer. The majority of cases (70%) are diagnosed in women aged 45 to 74, with the highest incidence occurring between the ages of 55 and 64. Statistically, 1 in 40 women will be diagnosed with endometrial cancer. Early-stage diagnosis significantly improves survival rates, as is the case with all cancers. The Tao Brush biopsy is capable of detecting endometrial adenocarcinoma, which accounts for 97% of all endometrial cancers. Because this method collects samples from the entire uterine lining with minimal discomfort to the patient, it is an excellent tool for early detection. Currently, it is the only available method for this purpose. The procedure for the Tao Brush biopsy is as follows: 1. The patient is positioned on the examination table with their feet in stirrups, similar to a routine pelvic exam. 2. The Tao Brush is inserted into the uterus, with a protective sheath in place to prevent contamination from cervical tissue. 3. Once the brush is correctly positioned, the sheath is removed. 4. The brush is rotated 4 to 5 times to collect tissue from the entire uterine lining. 5. The sheath is then replaced to ensure the collected tissue remains securely on the brush. 6. The brush is removed and immediately placed into a fixative solution. The entire procedure takes approximately 30 seconds and can be performed during a routine Pap smear. The collected sample is ready for processing within about 30 minutes and can be stored for several weeks, allowing for transport to an offsite laboratory. Currently, Bostwick Laboratories is the only facility processing Tao Brush biopsies, referred to as the TruTest. Results are typically available within three business days. In addition to early detection of endometrial cancer, the TruTest also screens for Chlamydia, Gonorrhea, and HPV.
